simple_definition: A four-digit US government number that says what kind of business a company is in; the SEC still tags every filer with one.
technical_definition: Standard Industrial Classification code; replaced by NAICS for US statistics in 1997 but retained by SEC EDGAR to describe filers and assign review offices.
example: NVIDIA is SIC 3674; Lam Research is SIC 3559.

simple_definition: The permanent ID number the SEC gives every company or person that files with it.
technical_definition: Central Index Key: 10-digit identifier (with leading zeros) used in EDGAR URLs and APIs, e.g. data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json.

simple_definition: A way of tagging each number in a financial report so computers can read it directly.
technical_definition: eXtensible Business Reporting Language, XML-based; required by the SEC since 2009 (now mostly inline XBRL); facts tied to US-GAAP or IFRS taxonomies. Also used by EDINET and DART.

simple_definition: The yearly report that foreign companies listed in the US file with the SEC, in English.
technical_definition: Annual report/registration form for foreign private issuers under the Exchange Act; due within four months after fiscal year-end; filed on EDGAR.

simple_definition: A big US-listed company that must file its annual report fastest (within 60 days).
technical_definition: SEC Rule 12b-2 filer category determining 10-K deadlines (60/75/90 days) and shown in EDGAR submissions metadata ('category').

simple_definition: Taiwan-listed companies must publish last month's sales by the 10th of each month, which gives an early look at chip demand.
technical_definition: Monthly operating revenue (consolidated under IFRS) input into MOPS before the 10th of the following month under Securities and Exchange Act Art. 36; unaudited. Local-language name(s): 月營收.

simple_definition: Taiwan's official website where listed companies post their financial reports, monthly sales and important news.
technical_definition: Market Observation Post System run by TWSE and TPEx under FSC supervision; English version e-MOPS. Local-language name(s): 公開資訊觀測站.

simple_definition: A Taiwan trading board for companies not yet fully listed; many young chip firms trade there first.
technical_definition: Taipei Exchange's emerging stock market (興櫃); stocks classified by the same industry groups as TWSE/TPEx. Local-language name(s): 興櫃.

simple_definition: South Korea's government website where companies publish their official filings.
technical_definition: Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System run by the Financial Supervisory Service; OpenDART API (40-character key) gives XML filings, XBRL financials and company industry codes. Local-language name(s): 전자공시.

simple_definition: Japan's government website where companies file their official annual and half-year reports.
technical_definition: FSA's electronic disclosure system under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act; API v2 with key; documents viewable for about 10 years.

simple_definition: The main yearly report a Japanese listed company files with the regulator, similar to a US 10-K.
technical_definition: 有価証券報告書 (yūka shōken hōkokusho) filed on EDINET under the FIEA; statutory viewing period 5 years plus 5-year extension. Local-language name(s): 有価証券報告書.

simple_definition: A Chinese website approved by the securities regulator where listed companies publish official announcements.
technical_definition: 巨潮资讯网 (www.cninfo.com.cn), a CSRC-designated information-disclosure website. Local-language name(s): 巨潮资讯网.

simple_definition: Shares of mainland Chinese companies traded in yuan on the Shanghai, Shenzhen or Beijing exchanges.
technical_definition: RMB-denominated ordinary shares listed on mainland exchanges; disclosure in Chinese via CSRC-appointed media.

simple_definition: A Shanghai stock board for technology companies; it holds the largest group of listed Chinese chip companies.
technical_definition: Sci-Tech Innovation Board of the Shanghai Stock Exchange, launched 13 June 2019; 588 companies and 119 IC companies as of June 2025. Local-language name(s): 科创板.
example: CXMT listed on the STAR Market in 2026.

simple_definition: Hang Seng's system for sorting Hong Kong-listed companies by industry; it has a semiconductor sector.
technical_definition: Hang Seng Industry Classification System: 12 industries, 31 sectors, 114 subsectors; semiconductors 703010, semiconductor equipment & materials 703020; revenue-based.

simple_definition: A private industry-sorting scheme from MSCI and S&P used by investors; chip firms are in 4530 'Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment'.
technical_definition: Global Industry Classification Standard; sub-industries 45301010 Semiconductor Materials & Equipment and 45301020 Semiconductors; 60% revenue rule; licensed data.

simple_definition: Hong Kong listing rules that let specialist tech companies, including some chip firms, list before they have big revenues.
technical_definition: HKEX Main Board Chapter 18C (Specialist Technology Companies); pre-commercial issuers carry a 'P' marker in their stock names.

simple_definition: Filings that tell the public when big shareholders or directors buy or sell a Hong Kong-listed company's shares.
technical_definition: Notices under Part XV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance, filed electronically via HKEX's DION system since 3 July 2017 and published on HKEXnews.

simple_definition: A Japanese IPO route that lets a company file its offering document before the exchange approves the listing, to sound out investors earlier.
technical_definition: Pre-approval securities registration statement (承認前届出書) introduced October 2023; Kioxia (Dec 2024) was the first IPO to use it. Local-language name(s): 承認前届出書.

simple_definition: A complete count and list of all companies in an industry, not only the famous ones.
technical_definition: Enumeration of every entity per role and country, combining official classification lists, filing-text searches, association directories and government lists, deduplicated by legal entity.

simple_definition: A non-US company listed in the US that follows lighter SEC rules, such as yearly Form 20-F instead of quarterly 10-Qs.
technical_definition: SEC status under Exchange Act Rule 3b-4; files 20-F annually (within four months) and 6-K for interim information.

simple_definition: A report Japanese listed companies file after the first half of their year; it replaced the legal quarterly report in 2024.
technical_definition: 半期報告書 under amended FIEA Art. 24-5 from 1 April 2024, due within 45 days (60 days for some companies). Local-language name(s): 半期報告書.
